The controller's destroy action (`host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy`) can raise on a nil host, so a failed DELETE leaves the admin with no feedback after confirming. When the DELETE fails (the 500 from the unguarded nil host in the controller, or a stale-id rejection), the admin gets no feedback and the row remains in the table, so the failure presents as the confirm dialog doing nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action does `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` with no rejection handling, unlike `save()` which has `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE request fails, there is no user feedback and no state rollback. This failure is plausible from the diff because `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately calls `host.destroy` without guarding against `nil`, which can raise and produce a 500. In that case, `deleteHost` is never sent, so the row stays and the confirm appears to do nothing.
